_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 natively to contract v3, mirroring the Dubai v3 fleet-investors structure per the international addendum (Saudi run — tourism-weighted utilization stack; Red Sea experiences are the headline layer). Sources: jeddah/REVENUE-INPUTS-JEDDAH.md + FARE-BENCHMARKS-JEDDAH.md + CREW-COST-BENCHMARKS-JEDDAH.md + DEMAND-POOLS-JEDDAH.md + AUTHORITY-MAP-JEDDAH.md + SPEED-RULES-JEDDAH.md + NODES-JEDDAH.md. CONTRACT v3: only `title` (<=6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (<=140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. This is fleet financing only — equity/fundraise/counterparty content firewalls apply in full. Utilization-stack economics lead frame; upside rows render UNPRICED on this page (no sourced local rates) and are never summed into totals. NOTE: no REVENUE-STACK file exists for Jeddah — the scenario model in this file was assembled this pass from REVENUE-INPUTS band mid-points and the program's standard stack structure, then script-verified to $0 diff; every quantity assumption is stated in _internal and flagged for review. Berthing and insurance are UNSOURCED for Jeddah and are excluded from all totals, disclosed on-page (fn11). Demand pools are sourced visitor/resident flows, labeled indicative — no employer trackers exist on this run and no employer page exists (international addendum). No phasing or fleet-count section: no sourced Jeddah fleet plan exists in the research set, so none renders.

fn1.text: Experience and charter pricing is positioned against Jeddah's operating Red Sea leisure market: sunset cruise seats published at SAR 150–300 per person, shared reef-day seats at SAR 400–450, and premium 15-guest hulls reported near SAR 2,000 per hour.

fn2.text: Demand pool figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — sourced visitor and resident flows, not commitments or commercial relationships.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship, overnight cargo and event-week surge — render unpriced on this page and are never included in totals. All figures are US dollars; local benchmarks are cited in Saudi riyals at the pegged rate of 3.75 riyals per dollar.

fn4.text: All trip times are planned on a conservative basis: open-coast segments at the vessel's service speed, reduced speed inside Obhur Creek, port waters and every landing approach. Route terms — lanes, speeds and sailing hours — are set with the sailing permit; no faster allowance is assumed in base times.

fn5.text: Committed-seat and spot pricing are derived bands, not quotes — anchored just above the city's live water-taxi fares of SAR 25–50 per trip (a real municipal fare anchor on this same water) and 15–40% below equivalent ride-hail legs for the same cross-city trip. Pending confirmation.

fn6.text: Crew costs use a Saudi-adapted method: Kingdom-wide marine wage evidence for a two-person crew (captain + deckhand), with employment costs — social insurance, allowances, end-of-service — stated explicitly. Every scenario prices crew at the mid benchmark of $33.50 per hour loaded; the low benchmark is $19.90, held out as cushion.

fn7.text: Spot-seat lines are computed as fill rate × residual commute seat-legs × fare, with seats sold rounded down to whole seats; the stated seat count × fare is the exact revenue line.

fn8.text: The conservative case assumes deliberately thin fills and pays back in about 16.5 years — shown as the floor, not a financing case.

fn9.text: A 12-month operating year on warm Red Sea water. June–September heat shifts midday leisure toward morning and evening slots — the city's own water taxi ran afternoon-to-late-night hours — and in Ramadan the service day compresses toward the evening. Scenario counts are annual monthly averages with that shape absorbed.

fn10.text: Energy is priced at the Kingdom's published commercial electricity tariff — SAR 0.32 per kWh, about $0.085 — roughly $0.35 per nautical mile for the vessel. At the program's standard $0.30 per kWh planning rate the energy line rises about 3.5×, and every scenario remains cash-positive.

fn11.text: Marina berthing and hull insurance are not included in these totals: Jeddah commercial berth rates and Saudi marine insurance quotes are unpublished, and placeholders are not used. Quotes are the open item — net figures and payback will tighten downward once they are added.

fn12.text: Jeddah Central is a published SAR 75 billion waterfront program including a marina and pier. It renders as roadmap reach only — no demand is modeled on it and nothing on this page relies on its completion.

copy.body: A commuter-only vessel earns in a fraction of its available hours — this network monetizes the whole day, twelve months a year. Committed seats form the schedule spine; Red Sea experiences and charters are the headline layer that carries the payback, priced against a leisure market Jeddah already clears at scale.

_internal.sources: REVENUE-INPUTS-JEDDAH.md (bands, season shape, cost inputs). Crew: CREW-COST-BENCHMARKS-JEDDAH.md (SAUDI-ADAPTED, LOW $19.9 / MID $33.5; instruction: MID in all tiers, LOW as sensitivity fn6). Energy: SEC/SERA commercial >6,000 kWh/mo = SAR 0.32/kWh = $0.0853/kWh; $/nm = 4.1 kWh/nm × $0.0853 = $0.34973 (cheaper sourced local tariff used per addendum rule).

opex_basis.crew: Per-scenario activity: 25 service days/mo × 8/10/12 crew-hours/day = 200/250/300 hrs × $33.5/hr MID = $6,700/$8,375/$10,050. Activity-hours basis authored this pass (commute weekdays + leisure weekends) — flagged for review.
opex_basis.energy: Distance basis: commute 176 legs × 10.0 nm (Al-Balad↔JYC express) = 1,760 nm + experiences (20/40/60 sailings × 15 nm) + charters (8/16/30 hrs × 12 nm/hr) = 2,156/2,552/3,020 nm × $0.34973 = $754/$893/$1,056 (rounded to whole dollars). Sensitivity at $0.30/kWh ($1.23/nm): line rises ~3.5×; nets stay positive in all scenarios (fn10).
opex_basis.maintenance: $82.5K/yr = $6,875/mo, program-consistent N45 figure, flat across scenarios.
opex_basis.berthing_insurance: EXCLUDED from totals — Jeddah commercial berth rates unpublished (JYC/Red Sea Marina quotes to obtain) and no Saudi marine insurance quote found; placeholders not used per fail-closed rule. Disclosed on-page via the null-value opex row + fn11. Payback will lengthen when quotes land.

_internal.opex_total_note: Opex varies by scenario (crew + energy scale): $14,329 / $16,143 / $17,981 — rendered as the conservative-to-upside band. Scenario nets reflect per-scenario opex.

layer_pricing_basis.committed_bundles_L1: DERIVED band $550/$650/$750 per seat-month per REVENUE-INPUTS (recommended band). Anchors: water-taxi SAR 25–50/trip (live municipal fare anchor — a STRENGTH, cited in fn5); $650/mo ≈ SAR 55/leg at 44 legs, just above the SAR 50 ceiling, 15–40% below ride-hail SAR 55–90/way; GASTAT wage context supports. Pending Jaideep confirmation.
layer_pricing_basis.spot_seats_L2: $16/$20/$24 per leg = SAR 60/75/90 — exactly the sourced JED-1 full-spine band in REVENUE-INPUTS. Fill 10/20/30% of residual seat-legs. Residual = 3,520 total commute seat-legs (20 seats × 8 legs/day × 22 days) minus committed legs (24/32/36 seats × 44 legs = 1,056/1,408/1,584) = 2,464/2,112/1,936. Seats rounded down (246/422/580); seat count × fare is the exact line (fn7).
layer_pricing_basis.experiences_charters_L3: Experiences $40/$55/$70 pp = SAR 150/206/262.5 — inside the sourced sunset/corniche band SAR 150–300 pp (reef-day products SAR 350–450 pp sit above the band and are upside mix, not priced in). Sailings 20/40/60 per month × 12/14/15 seats. Charters $400/$525/$650 per hr = SAR 1,500/1,969/2,437.5 — inside the sourced N45-class band SAR 1,500–2,500/hr; hours 8/16/30.
layer_pricing_basis.upside_unpriced: Sponsorship UNSIZED by design (REVENUE-INPUTS U1); cargo UNSIZED (U2); Jeddah Season/F1 surge has no sourced fare numerics (FARE file: render qualitatively only) — all render unpriced, $0 in totals.

_internal.committed_seat_allocation: ALLOCATION ASSUMPTION (EP precedent — flagged for review): committed seats sold (24/32/36 per vessel-month) exceed the 20 physical seats because a committed seat is a monthly entitlement spread across 8 daily commute departures, not a dedicated chair. Peak-leg load at upside: 36 members × 2 legs/day ÷ 8 departures ≈ 9 riders/leg average — inside 20-seat capacity even with spot fill; capacity check passes.
_internal.scenario_qa: Mid ~4.6 yr is the honest headline WITH the berthing/insurance exclusion disclosed (fn11 on the opex rows, total and contract note). Conservative is cash-positive but slow (16.5 yr) — rendered with fn8 floor language. Cross-city comparisons never render.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 30 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 20 knots — lifted clear of the water for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional hulls. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

copy.note: A vessel is a network asset, not stranded in one market — the multi-city network is the residual-value story.
